stemEn: A 3-year-old boy presented with decreased urination. On examination, he had a palpable bladder that was dull to percussion. A VCUG image showed a dilated proximal (posterior) urethra. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: Poor urinary output/obstructive symptoms مع palpable bladder، ومع VCUG يظهر dilated and elongated posterior urethra؛ هذه hallmark لـposterior urethral valves في المصدر.
reasoningEn: The VCUG finding of a dilated posterior urethra in a boy with bladder-outlet obstruction is classic for posterior urethral valves.
incorrectOptionsAr: Bladder teratoma أو diverticulum لا يفسران الـclassic posterior urethral dilation pattern في VCUG.
clinicalPearl: PUV is an important congenital cause of lower urinary tract obstruction in boys and may present later with weak stream, UTIs, enuresis, or CKD.
diagnosticSteps: Link original VCUG image before publication
Assess renal function and upper urinary tract dilation

stemEn: A newborn was found to have left renal hydronephrosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار UPJ obstruction لأنه أشيع سبب antenatal hydronephrosis، والنمط النموذجي unilateral hydronephrosis مع عدم توسع ureter أو bladder وnormal contralateral kidney.
reasoningEn: Isolated unilateral hydronephrosis in a newborn is the recalled classic presentation of UPJ obstruction.
incorrectOptionsAr: MCDK يظهر multiple noncommunicating cysts/dysplastic kidney. PKD عادة bilateral cystic/enlarged renal disease. PUV يسبب lower urinary obstruction وغالبًا bilateral hydronephrosis/distended bladder in males.
clinicalPearl: UPJ obstruction is a common cause of antenatal hydronephrosis; postnatal ultrasound pattern helps distinguish it from distal obstruction.
diagnosticSteps: Further functional imaging as clinically indicated

subtopic: Vesicoureteral reflux prophylaxis after resistant breakthrough UTI
stemEn: A 2-year-old child known to have vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) grade II on cephalexin prophylaxis presented with UTI due to E. coli resistant to cephalexin. He was successfully treated with TMP/SMX. What is your recommendation upon discharge?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار تغيير prophylaxis إلى TMP/SMX لأن organism resistant للـcephalexin، ويذكر أن للأطفال ≥2 months يمكن استخدام TMP-SMX أو nitrofurantoin كخيارات prophylaxis أقل مقاومة من cephalosporins. لكن indication لاستمرار prophylaxis في grade II VUR نفسها تعتمد على age, toilet training, prior febrile UTI, scarring وbladder/bowel dysfunction، لذلك يحتاج السؤال current verification.
reasoningEn: Given breakthrough UTI with cephalexin-resistant E. coli, the source changes prophylaxis to an active agent, TMP/SMX, while modern indications for continuous prophylaxis in low-grade VUR remain risk-factor dependent.
incorrectOptionsAr: الاستمرار على cephalexin غير منطقي إذا كان organism المقاوم سبب breakthrough UTI. إيقاف prophylaxis قد يكون مناسبًا لبعض low-risk VUR cases، لكن المصدر لا يختاره هنا بسبب سياق breakthrough infection.
clinicalPearl: Continuous antibiotic prophylaxis for VUR is risk-stratified; breakthrough resistance should prompt reassessment of both drug choice and the ongoing need for prophylaxis.
managementSteps: Reassess indication for ongoing prophylaxis and bladder/bowel dysfunction

stemEn: A 3-year-old boy known to have vesicoureteral reflux grade IV had a DMSA scan showing two scars in the right kidney while the left kidney is normal. He is asymptomatic with a normal blood pressure. Which statement is correct regarding his condition?

options.text: He has very high risk to develop hypertension later in life
You have to consider left nephrectomy if??
He will not develop hypertension if his blood pressure is normal at age 8 years
There is high association between renin level and the development of hypertension

explanationAr: المصدر يختار A ويؤكد أن renal scarring يرتبط بخطر لاحق للhypertension/proteinuria، لكنه يذكر أرقامًا مثل 10–30% في children/young adults وليس بالضرورة 'very high risk' لكل طفل. كما يذكر عدم وجود correlation ثابت بين plasma renin activity وBP. لذا الفكرة الأساسية صحيحة—الندبات ترفع risk—لكن wording يحتاج مراجعة.
reasoningEn: The source supports a long-term hypertension risk after reflux nephropathy/renal scarring, but the phrase 'very high risk' appears stronger than the incidence figures quoted in the same explanation.
incorrectOptionsAr: Normal BP بعمر 8 سنوات لا يلغي خطر future hypertension. المصدر نفسه يذكر عدم وجود correlation موثوق بين plasma renin activity وBP. Option B ناقص وغير قابل للتفسير كما هو محفوظ.
clinicalPearl: Children with reflux nephropathy need long-term BP and proteinuria surveillance because hypertension can appear years later.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Option B is incompletely recalled. Source answer A; explanation quotes 10–30% pediatric/young-adult hypertension and no stable PRA-BP correlation.

stemEn: An infant died after birth. There was a history of severe oligohydramnios and lung hypoplasia, consistent with Potter sequence. What could be the underlying possible cause?
explanationAr: المصدر يضع D (PUV) كمفتاح، لكنه في الشرح يبدأ بأن bilateral renal agenesis هي classic cause لـPotter syndrome، ثم يوضح أيضًا أن severe bilateral CAKUT أو bladder outlet/urethral obstruction مثل PUV يمكن أن تسبب severe oligohydramnios وpulmonary hypoplasia. وبما أن bilateral renal agenesis غير موجودة في الخيارات، قد يكون D مقصودًا، لكن A (bilateral dysplastic kidneys) أيضًا ممكن biologically حسب الشرح. لذلك نضع السؤال conflicting.
reasoningEn: PUV can cause severe oligohydramnios and Potter sequence through bladder-outlet obstruction, but the source's explanation also lists bilateral renal dysplasia as a possible cause and identifies bilateral renal agenesis as classic, creating ambiguity among the preserved choices.
incorrectOptionsAr: Unilateral renal agenesis أو horseshoe kidney وحدهما لا يسببان عادة severe oligohydramnios/Potter sequence لأن وظيفة renal tissue كافية غالبًا. أما A وD فكلاهما قد يسببان severe bilateral fetal renal dysfunction حسب الشرح، لذا لا نحسم D كverified answer.
clinicalPearl: Potter sequence results from severe, usually bilateral fetal renal dysfunction or urinary tract obstruction causing prolonged oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Also recalled 2018; source key D but explanation also lists bilateral renal dysplasia as a Potter-sequence cause and classic bilateral renal agenesis is not among options.

stemEn: A picture of a newborn with absent abdominal wall muscles was provided, consistent with prune-belly syndrome. Which statement is true regarding prognosis?

options.text: Most of them will die in the first year of life
One third of them will have ESRD
One third of them will have liver failure

explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن نحو one third قد يموتون stillborn/early infancy بسبب pulmonary hypoplasia، بينما up to 30% من long-term survivors قد يطورون ESRD؛ لذلك الخيار B هو الأقرب لصياغة المصدر.
reasoningEn: The source states that up to about 30% of long-term survivors develop end-stage renal disease, while early mortality affects a different subgroup with severe pulmonary hypoplasia.
incorrectOptionsAr: ليس 'most' المرضى يموتون في السنة الأولى وفق أرقام المصدر؛ وliver failure ليست complication prognosis المميزة المذكورة.
clinicalPearl: Prune-belly prognosis is driven largely by pulmonary hypoplasia and renal dysplasia/urinary-tract dysfunction.
diagnosticSteps: Link original newborn image before publication

stemEn: A newborn was found to have the shown findings, consistent with prune-belly syndrome. What is your priority in managing this patient?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار preserve renal function كالأولوية، ويشرح أن management يركز على bladder emptying، prevention of UTI، ومعالجة obstruction/reflux للحفاظ على renal function. لكن بقية الخيارات والصورة غير محفوظة هنا، لذلك يبقى incomplete recall/image-dependent.
reasoningEn: The source frames preservation of renal function through management of obstruction, bladder emptying, reflux, and infection as the key priority.
incorrectOptionsAr: بقية الخيارات غير محفوظة في المصدر، لذلك لم تُختلق.
clinicalPearl: Renal outcome in prune-belly syndrome depends on baseline dysplasia and ongoing urinary obstruction, reflux, and infection.
